What Boston movers cost on a typical local move

A move from one Boston address to another is a local move, so Boston movers cost you by the hour for a crew and a truck. On a typical local move, each mover costs $50–$75 an hour, and the crew's rate is that times the number of movers. A 2-mover crew for a studio or 1-bedroom home charges $100–$150 an hour. A 3-mover crew for a 2-bedroom home charges $150–$225 an hour, and a 4-mover crew for a 3-bedroom home charges $200–$300 an hour.

In total, a typical local move of a studio costs $280–$740, a 2-bedroom home $720–$1,800 and a 3-bedroom home $1,150–$2,850. Each figure assumes 10 road miles, an off-peak date, no stairs and no extras such as packing or storage. They are national figures for a typical move, not Boston quotes. Boston movers cost more than these figures on most city moves, because the things that slow a Boston move down all add billed hours.

Why Boston movers cost more than a typical local move

On an hourly bill, time is money. A Boston move usually takes longer than a typical local move: older buildings, narrow streets, scarce parking and a citywide moving day all add hours. Here is where the extra Boston movers cost comes from, and what you can do about each part of it.

Moving around September 1

Most Boston leases turn over at the start of September, as the local moving rules below note, and the city's college students move in at the same time. That puts a large share of the city's moves into the last days of August and the first days of September. Crews and trucks book up weeks ahead, the best time slots go first, and Boston movers cost the most of the year. When you give the calculator a moving date from May through September, it prices the move as peak season.

The City eases the crunch a little. From August 31 to September 2, it blocks off some common moving locations for truck drop-offs, and those spots don't need a permit, according to the City's moving truck parking page. If you're moving to the North End in July or August, the City asks you to call before you apply for a permit, because feast road closures may affect your street (Moving Truck Permit FAQs). A short carry from a good spot keeps Boston movers cost down, even on the busiest weekend.

Walk-ups, triple-deckers and stairs

Much of Boston's housing is older: brownstones, row houses and three-family triple-deckers, many with no elevator and narrow, turning stairs. On a walk-up, the crew carries every box and every piece of furniture up or down each flight, and big pieces may need to come apart to fit. Each flight adds time. The calculator asks about stairs and adds crew time for them, so answer it honestly, and expect Boston movers cost more for a third-floor walk-up than for a ground-floor unit.

If your building has an elevator, ask the manager whether you need to book it for moving day, and whether the building wants a certificate of insurance from your mover. A crew waiting for a shared elevator is still on the clock, and that wait is part of what Boston movers cost you.

Parking the truck

If the truck can't park near your door, the crew walks every load farther, and the long carry adds to Boston movers cost by the minute. On the narrow streets of neighborhoods like the North End and Beacon Hill, a big truck may not fit at all, and the crew shuttles loads from a smaller vehicle. In Boston, you don't need a permit to park a moving truck, but a permit guarantees you a legal spot for moving day. A standard permit reserves two parking spaces for one day. The City charges a fee for it, and more when the spaces are metered; its moving truck page lists the current amounts.

  • The space you reserve must be a real, legal parking spot: residential, commercial or metered. A legal spot right outside keeps Boston movers cost lower than one down the block.
  • Once you have the permit and signs, you or someone local posts the signs and puts flyers on parked cars at least 48 hours before the move. The City notes that some third-party companies can post them for you (Moving Truck Permit FAQs).
  • The permits cover city-owned streets only. On a street owned by the state's Department of Conservation and Recreation, you ask DCR for a temporary access permit instead (Moving Truck Permit FAQs).
  • A moving container needs a permit applied for in person, with a letter of authorization from the container company (City of Boston).

How far ahead to apply is in the local moving rules below. A City of Boston permit covers Boston streets only, so if your other address is in Cambridge, Somerville, Brookline or another neighboring city, ask that city about parking for the truck. A reserved curb is one of the cheapest ways to keep Boston movers cost down on moving day.

Travel time across the city

For a move within Massachusetts, the state's Department of Public Utilities says hourly moves carry a travel-time charge on top of the time spent moving. It is based on the distance between where the truck loads and where it unloads (Moving Within Massachusetts). Boston traffic, one-way streets and roads a moving truck can't use all stretch that drive. The calculator's hourly view counts the truck's driving as crew time, so a longer route shows up in your range and in what Boston movers cost you.

Massachusetts rules that shape Boston movers cost

Every company that moves household goods from one place in Massachusetts to another must be licensed by the Department of Public Utilities (DPU), as the licensing panel below explains. That license also governs your bill, so it shapes what Boston movers cost in several ways:

  • Filed rates. Movers file their rates, called a tariff, with the DPU and may not charge more or less than the rates on file. The DPU publishes a list of the movers it regulates, with their tariffs.
  • Written estimates. The DPU says an estimate given by phone or email is non-binding. It calls a written estimate made after a visit to your home one of your best safeguards against overcharges, so get one from each mover before you compare Boston movers cost between companies.
  • The final bill. Whatever the estimate says, the DPU says your final bill is set by the hourly rate, the packing done and any other services. Ask about every extra charge before you book.
  • Damage cover. The DPU says a mover's base rate limits its liability to $0.60 per pound per article. Most movers let you raise the declared value, and items such as antiques or paintings may need separate cover.
  • The bill of lading. It is your contract with the mover. Before you sign it, check that it shows the mover's DPU license number.

Leaving Massachusetts? The DPU only covers moves within the state. A move that crosses a state line falls under the FMCSA, and before an interstate move the mover must give you the Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move booklet and the Ready to Move brochure. On a long-distance move, Boston movers cost what the weight of your shipment and the miles decide, not the hours.

A worked example of Boston movers cost: a 2-bedroom move

Say you're moving a 2-bedroom apartment from one Boston neighborhood to another. A typical local 2-bedroom move, at 10 road miles, off peak and with no stairs, costs $720–$1,800. In hours, that's a 3-mover crew at $150–$225 an hour for 4.5 to 8 hours. That is the baseline, before any of the things that make Boston movers cost more.

Now make it a real Boston move and watch what Boston movers cost climb. Put the date on September 1, give the new place a third-floor walk-up, and add packing. Each one pushes the price up:

  • the September date moves it into peak season;
  • the stairs add crew hours;
  • a packing service for a 2-bedroom home adds $500–$1,200;
  • a parking permit adds the City's fee but can save the crew a long carry.

Enter your ZIP codes in the calculator above with your real date and stairs to see how far each one moves your range. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to see the price, so you know what Boston movers cost for your move before you call anyone.

Ways to keep your Boston movers cost down

  • Move off peak. A date from October through April avoids peak-season pricing in the calculator, and a mid-month date avoids the September 1 rush.
  • Reserve the curb. The permit fee can be less than the extra time a crew spends carrying everything down the block.
  • Pack it yourself. Doing your own packing is the simplest cut to Boston movers cost. A medium moving box costs $1.82–$2.69 each, according to published retail prices. A packing service for a 2-bedroom home costs $500–$1,200.
  • Be ready when the crew arrives. Have boxes taped, labeled and stacked near the door, and drawers emptied, so the crew's hours go on carrying.
  • Hire labor only. If you drive a rental truck yourself, 2 movers to load and unload cost $320–$910 in all, off peak. A 15-foot truck rents for $29.95–$30.00 a day plus $0.69–$2.49 per mile, by published rental prices. Check your route first: the local moving rules below name a Boston road that moving trucks can't use.
  • Compare written estimates. Check each mover's filed rates on the DPU list before you choose.

Put those together, and a mid-month, off-peak move with a reserved curb, boxes packed ahead and two or three written estimates is the surest way to keep Boston movers cost close to the typical figures above.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • If you're moving household goods within Massachusetts, your mover must be licensed by the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities (DPU).
  • Reserve a parking space for moving day (City of Boston).
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 10 road miles, off peak: $58–$103 with a rental truck before help, $390–$1,380 with a container, and $720–$1,800 with full-service movers.
  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • Tip guides suggest $4–$15 per mover per hour: $16–$98 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $48–$294 for 3 movers.
  • More households moved to Suffolk County from Middlesex County, MA than from any other county in 2022-2023: 7,512.
  • In Boston, May, July and August are the mildest, driest months to move, by NOAA's 30-year averages.
  • Suffolk County had 24 moving companies with paid employees in 2023: 3.1 per 100,000 residents, against 2.8 across the US.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • Boston movers bill local moves by the hour, so stairs, a long carry from the truck and the drive between addresses all add to the cost.
  • The calculator prices a date from May through September as peak season, so a date from October through April gives you a lower range.
  • Within Massachusetts, a mover may not charge more or less than the rates it files with the DPU, so check written estimates against those rates.

Boston parking, permit and truck rules for moving day

Local rules change what Boston movers cost on the day: where the truck can park, which roads it can use and when the city fills up. Each rule below names its City source.

Reserve a parking space for moving day

A moving day parking permit isn't legally required, but the City recommends one in some neighborhoods; it reserves a parking space from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Apply online at least fifteen days before your move, or at the Parking Clerk's Office in City Hall at least three days before.

Source: City of Boston, checked 28 October 2026

Keep moving trucks off Storrow Drive

You can't drive moving trucks on Storrow Drive because of its low clearance. The height limit is 10 feet.

Source: City of Boston, checked 28 October 2026

Plan around the early-September lease turnover

Most leases in Boston turn over at the beginning of September. The City also notes temporary traffic and parking restrictions in certain neighborhoods.

Source: City of Boston, checked 28 October 2026

Tipping a Boston crew after a long carry

A tip isn't part of what Boston movers cost on the bill, but most guides suggest one. Work out a tip per mover by the hour or by the day, and add it to your budget.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Boston moving countdown, from first quote to keys

Planning early keeps Boston movers cost down, above all before September 1. Enter your moving date to see each task, from picking a date to confirming the booking, on the day it is due.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Paper or digital, keep every page a company gives you until the move is settled.

  • A second date gives you room if the company you want is booked.

  • Everything you leave behind is one less thing to pack, load and pay to move.

4 weeks before

  • Label each box with its room and what's inside.

2 weeks before

  • A clear answer helps you plan the day, and check the bill if you pay by the hour.

  • Get a name and a direct number, not only the main office line.

  • Plan how those will travel, or give them away before moving day.

1 week before

  • Keys, gate or door codes, and someone there to let them in.

  • Ask for a phone number that will be answered on moving day.

The day before

  • Eat down the frozen food in the weeks before, so little is left to throw away.

  • A change of clothes, toiletries and any medicine for the first night.

Moving day

  • Point out anything fragile, very heavy or going to a particular room.

After the move

  • Ask your state's motor vehicle office how long you have to do it.

  • Say what went well and what didn't; it helps the next person choosing.

Questions

Boston movers cost: what you'll pay and why FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

Why do Boston movers cost more around September 1?

Most Boston leases turn over at the start of September, so a large share of the city's moves fall in a few days. Crews book up early, and Boston movers cost the most of the year then. The calculator prices any date from May through September as peak season, so a date from October through April gives you a lower range.

How much should you tip movers in Boston?

Tipping is up to you, and it comes on top of what Boston movers cost on the bill. The tipping range most moving guides give is $10.00–$20.00 per mover for a half day of up to 4 hours, and $20.00–$65.00 per mover for each full working day. Tip toward the top of the range for a walk-up or a long carry from the truck.

How much does it cost to move a 1,000-square-foot apartment?

Movers price what you own, not floor area. As a rough rule of thumb, 1,000 square feet is often a 2-bedroom home, and a typical local 2-bedroom move at 10 road miles, off peak and with no stairs costs $720–$1,800. In a walk-up, Boston movers cost more than that, because stairs add hours. Choose your home size in the calculator for your own range.

What hidden costs should you ask a moving company about?

Ask whether the quote includes travel time, a minimum number of hours, stairs, a long carry from the truck, packing materials and any charge for heavy items. Hidden extras like these are where Boston movers cost more than the quote, so ask how the bill changes if the move runs over the estimated hours. Get the answers in writing before moving day.

How much do long-distance movers charge from Boston?

Long-distance moves are priced on weight and distance, not hours, so Boston movers cost far more for them than for a move across town. A typical 2-bedroom move of 1,000 road miles, off peak and with no stairs or extras, costs $2,600–$5,700, or about $2.60–$5.70 per mile. Enter both ZIP codes in the calculator for your own route.
